subject: series
synopsis: Hazuki Minase's manga following a die-hard Final Fantasy fan who, along with his sister, is transported into a Final Fantasy-style world and must use his encyclopedic game knowledge to survive. A love letter to the franchise that rewards fans with game references while building its own engaging isekai narrative with genuine emotional stakes.
author: Hazuki Minase

subject: series
synopsis: Kenjiro Hata's sweet newlywed comedy: teen genius Nasa Yuzaki marries Tsukasa, the mysterious girl who saved his life, and slowly learns her centuries-old secret.

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Abraham's faithful comic adaptation of Martin's epic fantasy, with Tommy Patterson's art rendering Westeros's dynastic power struggles in sequential form. A solid adaptation for fans of the source material who want a visual companion to the novels.
author: George R.R. Martin

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series following the Guardians of the Galaxy in episodic adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited vertical reading experience.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A BOOM Studios horror anthology collecting new takes on dark and unsettling stories from various creators, aimed at showcasing the breadth of modern horror comics storytelling. Quality anthology horror with diverse creative voices.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 series spotlighting Hellverine — the demonic entity that possesses Logan's body, combining Wolverine's ferocity with supernatural hellfire power, developed during Ben Percy's Wolverine run. A horror-tinged action series leaning into Logan's demonic counterpart as a distinct character with its own malevolent perspective.
author: Ben Percy

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Sebela's 2016 Injustice tie-in from Harley Quinn's perspective, covering the events of the first Injustice game from her viewpoint as she joins Batman's resistance.
author: Christopher Sebela

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Kim Yale's 1988 Manhunter: bounty hunter Mark Shaw, spun out of Millennium, takes jobs that tie into Suicide Squad's world.
author: Kim Yale, John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's mid-1970s series adapting classic works of literature — Treasure Island, The Invisible Man, The Time Machine, and others — into comics format with professional Marvel creative teams. A solid educational comics initiative in the tradition of Classics Illustrated, making canonical literature accessible to readers who might not otherwise encounter it.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's lighthearted Infinity Comics series following the cats of the Marvel universe in humorous slice-of-life adventures, featuring Chewie, Liho, and other famous Marvel cats.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Reiji Miyahara's hugely popular romantic comedy manga following broke college student Kazuya Kinoshita after he rents a girlfriend through an app and falls for her, navigating the gap between the staged relationship and genuine feeling. A crowd-pleasing romance that achieved significant cultural reach.
author: Reiji Miyahara

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's digital Infinite Comic format entry featuring Spider-Man in adventures formatted for vertical scrolling on devices, part of the Ultimate Spider-Man animated tie-in line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hergé's landmark Belgian comic series following the young journalist Tintin and his dog Snowy around the world — 24 albums of meticulously researched adventure, brilliant comic timing, and extraordinary geographical and historical scope.
author: Hergé

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series featuring backup stories and team-up adventures involving the extended Batman supporting cast, including Robin, Batgirl, Man-Bat, and others. Published in the 1970s during the Batman Family era of DC.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Englehart's 1988 series spinning out of Millennium, following a multicultural team of heroes meant to represent a new stage of human evolution. Well-intentioned but widely regarded as awkward in execution.
author: Steve Englehart

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's samurai epic set in a fictional feudal Japan analog, following the warrior Obo-san who receives a sigil and is pulled between duty to his lord and a deeper spiritual path of justice. Written by Ron Marz with atmospheric art, it was one of CrossGen's more culturally specific entries, drawing on Japanese mythology and the samurai tradition.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis writes intimate, research-driven anthology stories about ordinary soldiers in World War II, emphasising the human cost of combat over heroism; widely praised as some of the finest war comics ever written.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's martial arts adventure series following Boon Sai Hong, a thief in an ancient China analog who accidentally bonds with the Mystic Ring and is reluctantly drawn into a destiny larger than himself. Written by Chuck Dixon with fluid action sequences, it was a crowd-pleasing genre exercise within CrossGen's interconnected sigil universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen's 2009 Doom Patrol: Robotman, Negative Man and Elasti-Woman back on Oolong Island, with Metal Men backups.

subject: series
synopsis: Remy LeBeau's various solo series. The character works better as a supporting player; extended solo outings struggle to sustain interest despite a charismatic protagonist.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Mike W. Barr's 1985 series following Batman's non-JLA team of Geo-Force, Halo, Katana, Metamorpho, and Black Lightning, a fun Bronze Age team book that spawned several revivals.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Masterson's Thor spin-off. Tom DeFalco and Ron Frenz create a workmanlike superhero series; Thunderstrike is a less compelling protagonist than Thor but has a loyal fanbase.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Len Wein and Paris Cullins's 1986 Blue Beetle: inventor Ted Kord's DC solo series after the Charlton heroes joined DC.

subject: series
synopsis: Top Cow's The Darkness: mob hitman Jackie Estacado inherits an ancient demonic power that manifests in shadow.

subject: series
synopsis: Sara Pezzini, a New York City detective, becomes the wielder of the Witchblade, an ancient supernatural weapon that bonds with her and grants extraordinary power while drawing her into a world of mystical conflict.
author: Marc Silvestri

subject: series
synopsis: The 1999 Batman Beyond ongoing based on the cartoon: Terry McGinnis as Batman in Neo-Gotham under Bruce Wayne's guidance.

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's 2022 X-Men Red: Storm and Magneto build a society on Arakko, terraformed Mars, amid war with Genesis.
author: Al Ewing, Carolina Munhóz

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology series evolved from Solo Avengers (1987–1989) into Avengers Spotlight, providing dedicated space for second-tier Avengers members rarely seen in their own titles. Notable for extended spotlights on Hawkeye, Tigra, and others, offering character development for heroes otherwise confined to team books.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Avengers volume 6 (2016-2018): Mark Waid's team against Kang, then the weekly No Surrender by Ewing, Waid and Zub, back to legacy #672-690.

subject: series
synopsis: The 2010 relaunch of Marvel's all-ages Spider-Man line, single-issue adventures of a teen Peter Parker.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Tobin's all-ages 2010 team-up series pairing Spider-Man with a different Marvel hero each issue.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom! Studios' 2016 Mighty Morphin Power Rangers relaunch: Kyle Higgins's Green Ranger arc, then Ryan Parrott's Necessary Evil and Coinless saga.
author: Kyle Higgins, Ryan Parrott

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Leonardo Manco's 2009 War Machine: James Rhodes wages a brutal one-man war on global injustice during Dark Reign.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Azzarello's 2005 Vertigo western: Confederate veteran Wes Cutter returns to Blackwater, Missouri, to take revenge under Union occupation.

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott, Christos Gage, and Giuseppe Camuncoli's era of the Amazing Spider-Man title follows Parker Industries' global expansion, delivering inventive globe-trotting adventures that culminated in the Clone Conspiracy event before returning Peter to his neighbourhood roots.
author: Dan Slott

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's monthly (1979-1983), mostly reprints, notable for the Captain Britain strip by Dave Thorpe and Alan Davis, then Alan Moore.
author: Dave Thorpe, David Michelinie

subject: series
synopsis: Kafka Asagiri and Sango Harukawa's manga: orphan Atsushi Nakajima joins the Armed Detective Agency, whose members wield powers named for famous writers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's reprint series collecting the classic Stan Lee and Steve Ditko / John Romita era Amazing Spider-Man stories, making foundational Silver Age material accessible in collected editions.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's trade paperback reprint line collecting extended runs of Avengers stories in thematic volumes, offering accessible entry points into decades of Earth's Mightiest Heroes adventures.
author: Roger Stern

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology horror-parody comic based on The Simpsons' annual Halloween episodes, featuring multiple short stories of supernatural mayhem, movie parodies, and dark comedy starring Springfield's favorite family.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Lutes' decades-in-the-making graphic novel trilogy depicts the fall of the Weimar Republic through the interwoven lives of Berlin residents from 1928 to 1933; a patient, deeply researched historical masterwork.
author: Jason Lutes

subject: series
synopsis: Josh Trujillo and Adrián Gutiérrez's 2023 Blue Beetle: Jaime Reyes, fresh from Graduation Day, defends Palmera City with family and friends.

subject: series
synopsis: Dennis Hopeless's series reuniting Cable with a ragtag team including Colossus and Dr. Nemesis, using a nonlinear narrative structure to tell a story about a team forced to commit crimes to prevent greater disasters.
author: Dennis Hopeless

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's Crossed spinoff following a psychopathic serial killer who discovers new opportunities in the Crossed apocalypse — transgressive even by Crossed standards.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: Reprint collection of Joe Kelly's landmark Deadpool run from the late 1990s, which transformed the character from a minor villain into a beloved antihero with fourth-wall-breaking humor and surprising emotional depth.
author: Joe Kelly

subject: series
synopsis: Pat Shand's Black Mask Studios series following a queer young woman in New York City who can grant wishes — a coming-of-age fantasy about identity, power, and figuring out what to do with supernatural gifts when you're still figuring out yourself.
author: Pat Shand

subject: series
synopsis: Q Hayashida's gloriously deranged fantasy set in a decrepit urban hellscape where a man with a lizard head searches for the sorcerer who transformed him. Dark, funny, and crammed with inventive worldbuilding — an underground cult classic that earned mainstream recognition.
author: Q Hayashida

subject: series
synopsis: DC series following Jared Stevens, a new host for the shattered Helm of Fate — a more street-level, attitude-heavy replacement for Doctor Fate aimed at the Image era's aesthetic. One of several DC mystical character revamps of the mid-1990s; the series ran 22 issues before cancellation.
author: John Francis Moore

subject: series
synopsis: An authorized fanzine and critical companion to Dave Sim's Cerebus, covering the ongoing epic's storylines, production history, and controversies through essays, interviews, and commentary. Essential reading for dedicated Cerebus scholars and those interested in the business and creative history of independent comics.
author: John Thorne

subject: series
synopsis: A series following Luke Cage and Iron Fist as they rebuild Heroes for Hire, blending classic street-level superhero action with the partnership dynamic that made Power Man and Iron Fist one of Marvel's most beloved duos.

subject: series
synopsis: A young boy is haunted by the ghost of a Heian-era Go master who yearns to achieve the 'Divine Move,' leading Hikaru to become a dedicated player. Hotta and Obata's series revitalized interest in Go worldwide and remains one of the best sports manga ever created.
author: Yumi Hotta

subject: series
synopsis: Skottie Young's ultraviolent fairy-tale comedy: Gertrude, trapped as a child in Fairyland for decades, hacks her way through its candy-colored inhabitants.
author: Skottie Young

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's Incredible Hulks (2010-2011): Bruce Banner leads a family of Hulks — Skaar, She-Hulk, Red Hulk — through Chaos War and World War Hulks.

subject: series
synopsis: Raule and Roger Ibanes' Barcelona-set crime comic following Jazz Maynard, a trumpet player with a violent past, through noir adventures in the city's criminal underworld — stylishly drawn with evocative atmosphere.
author: Raule

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's hardcover reprint series collecting the classic Lee/Kirby Thor stories from Journey into Mystery and Thor, preserving the mythological grandeur and cosmic adventure of the character's defining early years.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Reed's 2006 Ms. Marvel: Carol Danvers strives to become the best hero she can be, through Civil War and Secret Invasion.
author: Brian Reed

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino's 2016 Old Man Logan: the aged Logan of the Wasteland, stranded in the present, tries to stop his future.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's comic adaptation of PopCap's tower-defense game, following Patrice and her neighbors battling Dr. Zomboss's undead army. Light, funny all-ages adventure that captures the game's cheerful absurdity.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: Kaare Andrews's 2024 sequel to Spider-Man: Reign, returning to his dystopian future New York and an aged Peter Parker.

subject: series
synopsis: Micah Ian Wright's post-Authority Wildstorm series following a team of regular humans using military tactics to handle super-powered threats, a grounded political take on the Stormwatch concept.
author: Micah Ian Wright

subject: series
synopsis: Satoshi Miyagawa and Kai Kitago's charming DC manga in which Clark Kent, when not saving the world as Superman, quietly explores the diverse food culture of Japan. A delightful fusion of superhero and food manga sensibilities — each chapter pairs a small human moment with a lovingly depicted dish — that found readers far beyond typical Superman fans.
author: Satoshi Miyagawa

subject: series
synopsis: Stephen Murphy and Michael Zulli's thoughtful environmental sci-fi follows a young man tending to genetically engineered animals in a near-future world after an ecological catastrophe — Zulli's photorealistic animal art is extraordinary.
author: Stephen Murphy

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Hastings's meta-comic about Gwen Poole, a comics fan who finds herself inside the Marvel Universe and must use her genre knowledge to survive. Sharp, funny, and surprisingly touching with excellent art by Gurihiru.
author: Christopher Hastings

subject: series
synopsis: A DC series starring Lar Gand (Mon-El), a Daxamite hero who joins Earth's defense against alien threats while struggling with lead-based vulnerability. Bridges Legion of Super-Heroes mythology with post-Crisis DC continuity, with later issues tying into Zero Hour.
author: Robert Loren Fleming

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's digest-format anthology reprinting classic Disney comics stories featuring Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck, Goofy, and other Disney characters, making decades of Carl Barks and Floyd Gottfredson stories available in a convenient pocket format. A fine example of the digest comics tradition that flourished in the 1960s–1970s.
author: Various (Carl Barks, Floyd Gottfredson)

subject: series
synopsis: Alyssa Wong's 2023 Captain Marvel: Carol Danvers is bound to the mysterious Omen and the young Yuna Yang in The Omen and The Undone.

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Gray and Jimmy Palmiotti's 2006 Heroes for Hire: Colleen Wing and Misty Knight lead a mercenary super-team during Civil War.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's 1995 Punisher: Frank Castle becomes head of a Mafia family to destroy it from within.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1990 Superboy series tied to the live-action TV show, with Clark at Shuster University.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Loo's 2024 Dazzler mini: Alison Blaire's comeback world tour is sabotaged after the fall of Krakoa.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2012–2014 anthology series pairing individual Avengers and X-Men characters in double-length team-up stories following the Avengers vs. X-Men event. A lightweight but entertaining showcase format giving creators room to explore odd-couple dynamics without continuity weight.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Osamu Tezuka's foundational science fiction manga about a robot boy with the heart of a human child, exploring prejudice, the definition of life, and the relationship between humanity and technology. The cornerstone work of modern manga.
author: Osamu Tezuka

subject: series
synopsis: Christos Gage and Mike McKone's Marvel series follows a class of troubled young superhumans — secretly recruited because the Avengers judged them most at risk of becoming villains — as they train, rebel, and struggle to define themselves. A character-driven teen-hero drama.
author: Christos Gage

subject: series
synopsis: The Avengers annuals (1967-1994): Starlin's Thanos finale with Spider-Man in #7, Rogue's debut in #10, and assorted crossovers.
author: Fabian Nicieza, Mark Gruenwald

subject: series
synopsis: In a world of anthropomorphic animals where carnivore-herbivore tensions define society, a grey wolf named Legoshi navigates high school drama, forbidden desire, and his own predatory instincts. Itagaki uses her animal world to examine social hierarchies, identity, and the ethics of longing.
author: Paru Itagaki

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Welz's long-running underground/alternative adult comic Cherry Poptart (later just Cherry) — a sexually explicit humor comic following the misadventures of a cheerfully hypersexual young woman. One of the more successful adult underground comics of the 1980s–1990s, appreciated for its consistent comedic tone and Welz's clean, energetic cartooning style.
author: Larry Welz

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's breakout character — a sardonic, heavily-armed mechanoid mercenary — in his own series. Death's Head appeared across Marvel continuity and Doctor Who before his own ongoing; Simon Furman's dry wit makes the character memorable.
author: Simon Furman

subject: series
synopsis: Akira Toriyama and Toyotaro's manga continuation of the Dragon Ball story, set after the Majin Buu saga and covering the events of the Dragon Ball Super anime (and beyond) in manga form. Toyotaro's art captures Toriyama's style while the storylines expand the universe with new gods, universes, and power scales.
author: Akira Toriyama, Toyotarou

subject: series
synopsis: Tiziano Sclavi's landmark Italian horror comic follows Dylan Dog, an 'investigator of nightmares' in London who solves supernatural cases — enormously popular in Italy for decades and influential on European horror comics.
author: Tiziano Sclavi

subject: series
synopsis: Alex Raymond's gorgeous space opera strip following polo player Flash Gordon, Dale Arden, and Dr. Zarkov in their battles against the tyrant Ming the Merciless on planet Mongo; enormously influential on science fiction.
author: Alex Raymond

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Mike Wolfer's occult-combat series following William Gravel, a British Special Air Service sergeant who is also a minor-level combat magician navigating a world of dangerous secret societies and murderous sorcerers. Gravel's brutal pragmatism — using both SAS tradecraft and dark magic — gives the series a unique flavor distinct from most urban fantasy.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Will Pfeifer's 2003 series exploring what ordinary people do when they get access to a magical device that grants superpowers for one hour, with dark and realistic consequences. An underrated anthology-style concept.
author: Will Pfeifer

subject: series
synopsis: Kengo Hanazawa's acclaimed horror manga follows a meek, delusional manga assistant navigating a zombie apocalypse that perfectly mirrors his own mental unraveling. Praised for its slow-burn realism and psychologically rich protagonist before the supernatural elements escalate.
author: Kengo Hanazawa

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spurrier's acclaimed Hellblazer revival for DC Black Label returns Constantine to America for a mystery involving vanishing people and strange folklore, capturing the conniving occult detective at his most morally compromised. One of the strongest Hellblazer runs in years.
author: Si Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Kirby's post-apocalyptic adventure series following the last boy on Earth through a world ruled by intelligent animals, a joyful and inventive riff on Planet of the Apes.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: The official publication of the Lucasfilm Fan Club ran from 1987 through the mid-1990s, bridging the gap between Return of the Jedi and the Special Editions with behind-the-scenes features, production news, and some comic strip content. A primary historical source for Star Wars fandom's dormant era.

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology publication centered on the classic MAD Magazine feature Spy vs Spy, originally created by Cuban cartoonist Antonio Prohías in 1961 as a Cold War satire of espionage. The Black and White spy duo's silent slapstick battles — each ending in one spy's temporary defeat — remain one of the most iconic recurring features in comics history.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1975–1977 anthology series that, starting with issue #3, became the first ongoing home for the original Guardians of the Galaxy — Vance Astro, Yondu, Martinex, Charlie-27, and Starhawk — in their 31st-century adventures. Essential reading for original-team Guardians fans and historically important as the team's first real showcase.
author: Steve Gerber

subject: series
synopsis: Action Lab's licensed series based on Full Moon's Puppet Master horror film franchise, following the living puppets Blade, Tunneler, Jester, and others in stories that expand the films' mythology. For fans of the films primarily.
author: Shawn Gabborin

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Bedard and Karl Moline's CrossGen horror-road-trip series following Cassie Starkweather, a young woman who can see the monsters that walk among us wearing human faces, hunted by both those monsters and the FBI. A propulsive, genre-savvy series that blended horror, action, and American highway mythology across its 22-issue run.
author: Tony Bedard

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Kubert and Robert Kanigher's Easy Company is among the finest war comics ever produced — gritty, humanistic, and consistently anti-war in spirit despite its genre. Kubert's art is unmatched in the genre.
author: Joe Kubert

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's acclaimed 22-issue anthology series telling Spider-Man stories from the perspectives of people whose lives intersect with the wall-crawler — criminals, victims, bystanders, and supporting characters — rather than from Peter Parker's point of view. Rotating creative teams produced remarkably consistent quality, with standout issues by Garth Ennis, Greg Rucka, and Darwyn Cooke.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Humphries' 'Legendary Star-Lord' series follows Peter Quill on solo space adventures between Guardians stories — rogue missions, a complicated romance with Kitty Pryde across the galaxy, and classic space-opera mishaps. Fun and light, a good showcase for the character.
author: Sam Humphries

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1995 anthology series featuring standalone Batman stories by rotating creative teams, allowing broader experimentation with the character and his world outside of ongoing continuity.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A DC digital-first anthology delivering short, accessible stories about the DC hero roster, designed as an entry point for new readers with varied creative teams and self-contained narratives.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Grell's fan-favorite 1976 series following USAF pilot Travis Morgan trapped in the underground world of Skartaris, a sword-and-sorcery adventure series with Grell's signature dynamic art.
author: Mike Grell

subject: series
synopsis: EC Comics' legendary science fiction anthology from the early 1950s, featuring stories by Al Feldstein and original tales inspired by the best SF of the era, with stunning art by Wally Wood, Al Williamson, Harvey Kurtzman, and Jack Kamen. Among the finest science fiction comics ever produced — daring, satirical, and humanist in ways that still resonate.
author: Al Feldstein

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Greg Capullo's Marvel miniseries unleashes a brutal, stripped-down Wolverine in a near-future where he is among the last heroes standing, cutting a bloody path toward revenge. A savage, stylized showcase.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: The comic tie-in to the acclaimed Disney+ revival animated series, continuing the adventures of the X-Men team from the beloved 1990s animated show. Bridges gap content and expands on plot threads from the revival series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel/20th Century Studios crossover pitting T'Challa against a Predator alien hunter in Wakanda. A natural genre mashup that leverages both characters' warrior instincts and technical sophistication.

subject: series
synopsis: John Arcudi and Tan Eng Huat's 2001 Doom Patrol: Robotman leads a new team of young misfits — Fever, Freak, Kid Slick and Fast Forward.

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1994 Ninjak: British agent and ninja Colin King battles corporate villains, later written by Abnett and Lanning.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's series following Nick Fury assembling a new team of young heroes while uncovering the shocking truth that HYDRA has been embedded inside S.H.I.E.L.D. since its founding. Intricate spy plotting with strong character work.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Acclaim's 1997 relaunch of the X-O Manowar armor for its rebooted universe.

subject: series
synopsis: John Rogers and Keith Giffen's 2006 Blue Beetle: El Paso teen Jaime Reyes bonds with the alien scarab and fights the Reach.

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay's 2024 Vengeance of the Moon Knight: after Marc Spector's death, a new Moon Knight stalks his city while Marc's allies investigate.

subject: series
synopsis: Dick Foreman's 1993 Vertigo Black Orchid ongoing, following Gaiman and McKean's plant-woman Susan Linden into ecological horror.

subject: series
synopsis: Ghost Rider (2006-2009): Daniel Way's Johnny Blaze escapes Hell, then Jason Aaron's grindhouse war against renegade angels.

subject: series
synopsis: Rainbow Rowell's 2023 Sensational She-Hulk, continuing Jen Walters's life in New York with Jack of Hearts.

subject: series
synopsis: Titan's 2024 revival of the black-and-white Conan magazine: new Howard-inspired sword-and-sorcery tales with text features.

subject: series
synopsis: Oni Press's 2025 Adventure Time series: Finn, Jake and the Land of Ooo in new adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's 2013 Mighty Avengers: Luke Cage leads a street-level team with Spider-Hero, White Tiger and Power Man.

subject: series
synopsis: Andy Diggle and Leandro Fernández's 2024 Elseworlds sequel to Gotham by Gaslight, introducing a Victorian-era Kryptonian.

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's 2018 Fantastic Four: the family returns to Earth, Ben marries Alicia and Doom and Galactus loom.
author: Dan Slott

subject: series
synopsis: A class of middle-school misfits must assassinate their superpowered octopus teacher — who is also their most dedicated and effective educator — before he destroys the Earth. Balances absurdist comedy with genuine emotional investment in every student's growth.
author: Yûsei Matsui

subject: series
synopsis: DC's digital-first anthology series set in Gotham City, featuring various creative teams telling character-focused stories about Batman and Gotham's residents during the COVID-era. A rapid-response digital publishing experiment that captured a snapshot of Gotham as a city under extraordinary stress.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Judd Winick's New 52 series introducing David Zavimbe as Batman's representative in Africa, tackling corruption and genocide in the Congo with superhero action.
author: Judd Winick

subject: series
synopsis: Pat Mills and Joe Colquhoun's harrowing World War I epic following young soldier Charley Bourne; widely regarded as one of the greatest British war comics ever made, combining meticulous historical research with genuine anti-war pathos.
author: Pat Mills

subject: series
synopsis: Deadpool crosses over with various Marvel heroes. The concept works better in short doses than extended runs; the best issues have genuine comedic timing.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Vado's 1995 series featuring a splinter group of Justice League members led by Captain Atom taking a more proactive, aggressive stance, a product of 90s extremism that is generally regarded as a low point of the era.
author: Dan Vado

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm anthology using the Gen 13 characters as a launching pad for alternative creative teams and experimental stories outside the main continuity. Each arc by different creators offered genre variations on the core Gen 13 cast.

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's 18 Days — Morrison's ambitious graphic novel retelling of the Mahabharata's Kurukshetra War, reimagining the great Indian epic as a techno-mythological conflict where gods and heroes wield baroque super-weapons. Morrison's cosmic sensibility made this a natural project, rendered in vivid detail by Graphic India's team.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Daimon Hellstrom solo series exploring the Prince of Lies in horror-supernatural adventures, part of the early 1990s horror-adjacent Marvel line. Atmospheric but inconsistent.
author: Rafael Nieves

subject: series
synopsis: Satoshi Miyagawa's absurdist manga comedy reimagines the Joker as an unlikely single father raising baby Bruce Wayne after the Waynes are killed. A wildly irreverent premise played with genuine warmth and slapstick invention.
author: Satoshi Miyagawa

subject: series
synopsis: The Legion of Super-Heroes (1980-1984): Paul Levitz and Keith Giffen's run including The Great Darkness Saga.
author: Gerry Conway, Paul Levitz

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages Marvel anthology. Paul Tobin's contributions especially are sharp and enjoyable — accessible superhero fun.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's hardcover reprint line collecting early Iron Man stories by Stan Lee and Don Heck, documenting the character's evolution from Cold War origin through his establishment as one of Marvel's premier heroes.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Yasuo Ohtagaki's brutal Gundam side-story set during the One Year War in the debris-field Thunderbolt Sector pits two ace pilots against each other in some of the most viscerally violent mecha combat in the franchise. Distinguished by its jazz-heavy aesthetic and unflinching depiction of war's cost.
author: Yasuo Ohtagaki

subject: series
synopsis: Ai Yazawa's celebrated josei manga follows two young women both named Nana who meet on a train to Tokyo and become unlikely roommates as they pursue love and rock stardom. Praised for its deeply human characters, authentic portrayal of adult relationships, and unflinching emotional honesty.
author: Ai Yazawa

subject: series
synopsis: Robico's talky high-school comedy: two classmates' rambling conversations about life and love slowly turn into romance.

subject: series
synopsis: Dale Keown's Image series featuring the massive alien-human hybrid Pitt in brutal action against various threats. Known primarily for Keown's striking character design; the plotting is secondary to the visceral spectacle.
author: Dale Keown

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Gruenwald's cosmic series starring Wendell Vaughn wielding the Quantum Bands, building Marvel's cosmic mythology while Gruenwald systematically catalogued and connected obscure Marvel lore. A labor of love for dedicated Marvel readers.
author: Mark Gruenwald

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1993 Secret Weapons: Dr. Eclipse assembles a covert team of heroes for missions in the Valiant universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's New 52 series following the former Green Lantern as an anti-hero rebuilding the Sinestro Corps while wrestling with his own convictions about fear and order in the universe.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: The iconic Belgian comic by Franquin and others, a cornerstone of European sequential art.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter's New Universe title about a motorcycle mechanic who receives the Star Brand, immense power he has no idea how to control, part of Marvel's ambitious but ultimately struggling 1986 New Universe initiative.
